messages:
Sam: hey all, Sam here (first day). trying to map who to ping for specific things so i don't spam. quick list: 1) owner for routing/fallback rules (e.g., downgrade to q4 model when Dedicated is full)? 2) who approves Dedicated console access & quota bumps? 3) who gets paged for production latency vs model-quality regressions? any short links or a tiny cheat-sheet appreciated. :wave:

Vera: welcome Sam! Routing + fallback rules live with eng-platform (they own policy, routing config, and regional failover). For model-quality regressions ping eng-ml first.

Josh: access/approvals: open the IT access form and include your manager as approver. For Dedicated capacity increases, submit the capacity request (it routes to eng-ops + finance). If you need temporary test access, add `temp_access: 24h` in the notes.

Access-bot: Access form link: https://internal.redwood.com/forms/dedicated-access. Ticket template available when you start a new IT request.

Rita: paging summary: P0/P1 perf or outage -> eng-sre oncall (pagerduty). eng-sre triages and escalates to eng-platform (capacity/routing) or eng-runtime (runtime/oom/batching) or eng-ml (quality). For anything customer-facing add `#customer-impact` and loop in CS.

eng-platform: tiny extra: if you plan experiments that change routing, open a short RFC and post in #eng-platform with the rollout window. For automated fallback changes we require a brief changelog entry and a rollback plan.

Sam: thanks! can someone paste a minimal access template i can copy into IT?

Josh: paste this into IT ticket:
```
Subject: Dedicated Console / Capacity Access - sam@example.com
Requester: Sam (sam@example.com)
Manager: <manager-name>
Team: <team-name>
Reason: Onboarding + need read access to Dedicated console to validate routing for feature X
Requested resources: console read, project <proj>
Expected peak QPS: 75
Temp access: 24h (if applicable)
Approvers: manager + eng-ops
```

Sam: filed the ticket and CC'd manager. appreciate the quick orientation! :sparkles: DMing if approver needs anything.
